subject: physics
title: Circular Motion & Gravitation Adventure 1: Circular motion essentials
welcome_lead: Today you'll whirl in a circle with centripetal force.
meta_desc: Physics — circular motion, angular velocity ω, centripetal a = v²/r, F = mv²/r.
final_note: You learned circular motion needs centripetal acceleration a = v²/r = ω²r toward centre; F = mv²/r supplied by tension, gravity, friction, normal etc.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Object moving in circle of radius r:

v = 2πr/T = ωr.
ω = 2π/T = 2πf.

Even at constant speed, the velocity vector keeps changing direction → acceleration!

Acceleration always toward centre:

a = v²/r = ω²r

From Newton 2: net force toward centre:

F = mv²/r

This is provided by gravity (orbit), tension (string), friction (car turning), normal (loop-the-loop) — never a separate 'centripetal' force itself.

Banking allows horizontal centripetal F from normal force without friction: tanθ = v²/(rg).

Vertical loop: at top, gravity + normal both centripetal; minimum speed when N = 0: v_min = √(rg).

Examples: F1 racetrack banking; roller coasters; whirling buckets.

Which of the following is a fundamental particle: proton, electron, or neutron?
options: The galaxies are turning red because they are getting older.
All three (proton, electron, neutron) are fundamental particles that cannot be broken down.
Only the proton is fundamental; electrons and neutrons are composite.

mcqs.q: Why does a metal spoon in hot water heat up faster than a wooden one?
options: Metal heats up faster because it has more thermal energy to begin with.
Metal heats up faster because it has a lower specific heat capacity, requiring less energy per degree.
Only the proton is fundamental; electrons and neutrons are composite.
Metals have higher thermal conductivity, so heat is transferred more rapidly through them.

mcqs.q: What does the cosmological redshift of distant galaxies indicate?
options: Galaxies are moving through space away from us, like objects flying outward from a centre.
Only the proton is fundamental; electrons and neutrons are composite.
Space itself is expanding, stretching the wavelength of light from distant galaxies as it travels.
The galaxies are turning red because they are getting older.
